methods.label: Apply the property theorem
methods.explanation: This is a property of a line parallel to a plane: the line of intersection is parallel to the original line.
methods.levelReason: This is a direct application of the property theorem in the supplied textbook scope.

methods.label: Use coplanarity and nonintersection
methods.explanation: Both \(a\) and \(b\) lie in the cutting plane, so they are coplanar. Since \(a\parallel\alpha\), no point of \(a\) lies in \(\alpha\). But \(b\) lies in \(\alpha\), so \(a\) and \(b\) have no common point. Coplanar lines with no common point are parallel. Thus \(a\parallel b\), choice C.
methods.levelReason: This derives the conclusion from elementary definitions that precede the property theorem.
